Now,

questions.question:
In the following question below are given some statements followed by some conclusions based on those statements. Taking the given statements to be true even if they seem to be at variance from commonly known facts. Read all the conclusions and then decide which of the given conclusion logically follows the given statements.

**Statements:**

I. All R are M.

II. Some S are R.

**Conclusion:**

I. Some R are S.

II. Some M are not R.

III. Some R are M.

options.text: Both conclusions I and III follows
Both conclusion I and II follows

questions.solution:
Given Statements:

I. All R are M.

II. Some S are R.

The least possible Venn diagram for the given statement is:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/682a1a60d8748fde8e91b2ea2c9b7c8f7b11b608dc17476c7af1d804762d38b0.png] 

Conclusions:

I. Some R are S - True (Because, Some S are R it also gives Some R are S).

II. Some M are not R - False (Because, All R are M gives Some M are R and no relation is given about the remaining part, so it can be possible only).

III. Some R are M - True (Because, All R are M it also gives Some R are M).

So, Both conclusions I and III follows.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question: Number of wickets taken by six bowlers Anil, Kamal, Laxman, Mohan, Bittu and Rahul are compared. Number of wickets taken by Kamal are more than only the number of wickets taken by Anil. Number of wickets taken by Bittu are less than only two bowlers. Number of wickets taken by Mohan are not more than Bittu. Who among the following has taken more wickets than Bittu?
questions.solution:
Given: Six bowlers Anil, Kamal, Laxman, Mohan, Bittu and Rahul.

1) Number of wickets taken by Bittu are less than only two bowlers.

_____ > _____ > Bittu > _____ > _____ > _____

2) Number of wickets taken by Kamal are more than only the number of wickets taken by Anil.

_____ > _____ > Bittu > _____ > Kamal > Anil

3) Number of wickets taken by Mohan are not more than Bittu.

Rahul/Laxman > Rahul/Laxman > Bittu > Mohan > Kamal > Anil

Here, Either Rahul or Laxman has taken more wickets than Bittu,

But, Laxman is not given in the option, so take 'Rahul' as the answer.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Option 1"**.

questions.question:
After interchanging the given two numbers, what will be the value of the given equation?

6 and 2 ; 9 ÷ 2 × 6 + 5 - 1
questions.solution:
BODMAS Table: 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/d50192f098c21078501d30eeafe1a8c64bc30dd9621c48caa8a39ffc60f68b64.png] 

Given Equation: 9 ÷ 2 × 6 + 5 - 1

After interchanging '6 and 2' we get;

⇒ __**9 ÷ 6**__ × 2 + 5 - 1

⇒ __**1.5 × 2**__ + 5 - 1

⇒ __3 + 5__ - 1

⇒ __8 - 1__ = 7.

Hence, the correct answer is "Option 2".

questions.question:
Eight boys Anil, Kamal, Ram, Sanjay, Aakash, Vivek, Rahul and Ramu are sitting around a circular table facing towards the centre (not necessarily in the same order). Vivek is second to the right of Anil. Anil is fourth to the right of Ramu. Sanjay is third to the right of Ram. Ram is not the immediate neighbour of Vivek or Kamal. Ramu is not the immediate neighbour of Rahul.

Who is the immediate neighbour of Anil and Ram?
questions.solution:
Given: Eight boys Anil, Kamal, Ram, Sanjay, Aakash, Vivek, Rahul and Ramu. 

1) Vivek is second to the right of Anil. 

2) Anil is fourth to the right of Ramu.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a3a66245b8d5f48c3c11dbdf0d4ade8d6ac27f03f535f119854d0ec7fe6033e.png] 

3) Ram is not the immediate neighbour of Vivek or Kamal.

4) Sanjay is third to the right of Ram.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a1c0ea9dfff10892658f29b0520551e777f0d14e748a6c90e310103c67c2fd81.png] 

5) Ramu is not the immediate neighbour of Rahul.

And, Aakash will sit on the remaining place.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/5bcbb3d7adbb16615bc79a1119d4643c8914e48bec65cbaa1fb77dcff3e729a5.png] 

Here, 'Rahul' is the immediate neighbour of Anil and Ram.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Rahul"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'FAN' is written as '21'. How will 'TORCH' be written in that language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Sum of the place values of the letters in the word is the code of that word.**

Now,

'FAN' is coded as '21'

⇒ F(6) + A(1) + N(14) = 21.

Similarly,

for **'TORCH' **

**⇒ T(20) + O(15) + R(18) + C(3) + H(8) = 64;**

So, 'TORCH' will be coded as '64'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"64"**.

questions.question: In a certain code language, 'GLOBE' is coded as '40', 'GRASS' is coded as '63'. What is the code for 'HANDY' in that code language?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **Sum of the place values - 1.**

Now,

'GLOBE' is coded as '40'

⇒ G(7) + L(12) + O(15) + B(2) + E(5) - 1

⇒ 41 - 1 = 40.

'GRASS' is coded as '63'

⇒ G(7) + R(18) + A(1) + S(19) + S(19) - 1

⇒ 64 - 1 = 63.

Similarly,

for **'HANDY' **

**⇒ H(8) + A(1) + N(14) + D(4) + Y(25) - 1 **

**⇒ 52 - 1 = 51;**

So, 'HANDY' will be coded as '51'.

Hence, the correct answer is **"51"**.

questions.question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth number in the same way as the second number is related to the first number and fourth number is related to third number.

11 ∶ 122 ∶∶ 14 ∶ 197 ∶∶ 18 ∶ ?
questions.solution:
The logic followed here is:

Logic: **(1st number)² + 1 = 2nd number.**

Now,

For, 11 : 122

⇒ (11)² + 1

⇒ 121 + 1 = 122.

For, 14 : 197

⇒ (14)² + 1

⇒ 196 + 1 = 197.

Similarly, for **18 : ?**

**⇒ (18)² + 1**

**⇒ 324 + 1 = 325.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"325"**.
